plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Reduce other leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet concentration limits.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
The remaining portfolio will be focused on broad index and quality names.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential ~1.5%/month return. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth.

plan: Trim SOXL, MUU, and SPAL to reduce leveraged ETF exposure and meet mandate.
Reduce METU, PLTU, and MSFU to lower overall leverage.
Maintain QQQI at 25% to keep income exposure.
Buy XLV at 4% to diversify into a high-scoring sector.
This plan balances risk and growth, reducing overall leverage while adding a new quality name.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets risk-first growth, aiming for ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a new, high-quality setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: Increase SOXL, MUU, and SPAL to 6% each, leaning into leveraged ETFs.
Increase METU, PLTU, and MSFU to 6% each, boosting leveraged exposure.
Maintain QQQI at 25% to keep some income exposure.
Buy XLV at 6% to add a high-scoring setup with increased size.
This plan aggressively uses leverage and concentrates in high-potential names.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4%/month. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this strategy carries substantially higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and daily decay from leveraged products. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Reduce other leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to boost income exposure.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
The portfolio will be heavily weighted towards income and broad index ETFs.
income.read: This income plan targets parking cash for yield, aiming for ~1%/month. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index. While focused on distributions, NAV can still fall in selloffs, and distributions are variable.
